comparison_note: All comparisons use completed days: yesterday (2026-08-02) is the run_date. Today is excluded as it is an incomplete day. Cell C Recharges compares yesterday against same-day-last-month and same-day-two-months-ago, plus MTD-vs-prior-MTD (same day-of-month cutoff, so periods are equal length). Note: 2026-08-02 is a Sunday, while 2026-07-02 (Thursday) and 2026-06-02 (Tuesday) are weekdays — weekday-vs-weekend mismatch is a likely contributor to the drops flagged below, on top of any genuine issue.

flags: Yesterday (2026-08-02) recharge revenue was R242,614.57, down 26.7% vs same day last month (R330,906.00) and down 20.5% vs same day two months ago (R305,170.00) — both breach the 20% drop threshold (count did not breach: down 18.0% and 13.0% respectively).
MTD recharge revenue (R558,325.89) is down 13.3% vs prior-MTD (R643,883.00), breaching the ±10% variance threshold. MTD count variance was 6.3% — within tolerance.
Same-day-last-month vs same-day-two-months-ago count varies 6.1% (20,594 vs 19,411), breaching the ±5% threshold.
Same-day-last-month vs same-day-two-months-ago value varies 8.4% (R330,906.00 vs R305,170.00), breaching the ±5% threshold.
Revenue sanity check passed for all periods — AVG per recharge ranged R14.37–R16.07, MAX ranged R300–R549, both within normal bounds. No exclusions applied.

Yesterday qty/value dropped >20% vs BOTH historical points: qty 19,108 vs 26,553 last month (down 28.0%) and vs 24,280 two months ago (down 21.3%); value R245,102.75 vs R357,170.12 last month (down 31.4%) and vs R322,116.75 two months ago (down 23.9%).
MTD vs prior-MTD variance breaches ±10% for both metrics: qty down 25.9% (49,810 vs 67,231), value down 54.6% (R757,074.45 vs R1,666,251.62).
Same-day-last-month vs same-day-two-months-ago variance breaches ±5% for both metrics: qty up 9.4%, value up 10.9%.
3-month trend abnormal: value leg (prior-MTD → current-MTD) moved -54.6%, well past the 25% single-leg threshold; qty leg moved -25.9%, just past the threshold.

Tenant breakdown for yesterday vs same-day-last-month shows the drop is broad-based, not concentrated in one tenant: uConnect R241,985.31 → R350,447.88 (-30.9%); ME&YOU R3,117.44 → R6,722.24 (-53.6%).

Revenue sanity check passed — per-row AVG ranged R12.24–R34.53 and MAX ranged R434.78–R1,532.84 across all 6 periods checked (Jun 1–Aug 2), no order-of-magnitude outliers. No exclusions applied. WhatsApp purchase columns excluded from all sums per known masking-policy artifact.

2026-08-02 also has notably fewer underlying rows (15,998) than 2026-07-02 (28,711) or 2026-06-02 (24,589) in the source table, consistent with the Sunday vs weekday mismatch noted in comparison_note rather than a processing failure.

New-subscriber volume dropped 67.6% vs day before (720 vs 2,225 on 2026-08-01) — breaches the 60% drastic-drop threshold. Likely partly explained by 08-02 being a Sunday vs 08-01 a Saturday, both lower-volume days, but the drop still trips the rule.
New-subscriber Active-1 count dropped 84.1% vs day before (77 vs 483), breaching the 60% threshold.
MTD Active-1 count among new subscribers dropped 78.3% vs prior-MTD (560 vs 2,583; rate 19.0% vs 44.7%), breaching the 60% threshold.
Day 2-4 registration-activity cohort (2,462) was 40.1% below the trailing 7-day average (4,109) — within the 60% tolerance, not flagged.
Day-30 Active-7 retention and never-used-vs-last-month comparisons are N/A: the snapshot log only goes back to 2026-07-21, so neither 2026-07-02 nor 2026-06-02 has a logged snapshot yet.

Spread between VW_ACTIVE_SUBSCRIPTIONS_USAGE_DETAILS (393,060) and the other two tables (DIM_SUBSCRIBERS 387,940; UCONNECT_MAY_MERGE uConnect-only 387,946) is 5,120 rows — well past the 15-row tolerance. DIM_SUBSCRIBERS and UCONNECT_MAY_MERGE agree closely with each other (spread of 6), so the discrepancy sits with the active-subscriptions usage view.
Duplicate checks are clean: 6 duplicated ACCOUNT_NUMBERs (12 rows) and 9 duplicated ICCIDs (44 rows) among active uConnect-only records — both well under the 100 threshold.
MTD terminations (20, covering 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-02) are below the threshold of baseline + 500 (1,580.5 + 500 = 2,080.5) — flags RED per the rule.

Known data-shape caveat: termination dates are batch-applied late in the month, not day-by-day. Full-calendar-month sanity check: July 2026 had 84,803 uConnect terminations total vs only 1,893 in its first 2 days; June 2026 had 72,486 total vs only 1,268 in its first 2 days. A near-zero count this early in August is consistent with that same batch pattern, not necessarily a processing outage — treat this RED with that context rather than as a standalone alarm.
